verdict.rationale: Hightouch's own documented architecture keeps customer data in the customer's warehouse rather than a proprietary store. Events land in your warehouse, and Identity Resolution writes queryable tables there. Workspace resources can be managed via Git Sync and a REST API, so leaving requires little data extraction. However, there is no documented export feature, no stated open file formats, and no documented path for exporting configuration such as audiences and journeys in full. Missing for 10: an explicit documented export/offboarding capability, named open formats for exported data and config, confirmation that all workspace objects (audiences, journeys, AI Decisioning agents) are exportable, and independent hands-on corroboration of a clean exit.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can export all of my data in open formats and leave

citations.quote: It runs on top of your data warehouse, so teams can use customer data without copying it into a separate system.
Hightouch Events collects customer behavior from websites, mobile apps, and backend systems, then stores that data in your warehouse.
Query these directly, build models on them in Customer Studio, or sync them downstream.
Git Sync lets you manage workspace resources programmatically.
Hightouch's hybrid architecture stores no data in Hightouch itself out of the box—it all stays in the customer's own warehouse/S3 bucket
